mainEntity.name: How does an access control system work?

acceptedAnswer.text: An access control system validates an individual’s identity through credentials like a card or PIN. Once the identity is validated against the pre-set permissions, the system will either grant or deny access. Access control systems don’t just limit access to physical areas; they can also protect digital assets like networks, files and data. Additionally, access control systems offer a pathway to automating your property for energy saving initiatives, allowing you to control lights, air conditioning and more.

mainEntity.name: Are access control systems easy to use and manage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Despite their sophisticated technology, access control systems are designed to be user friendly. From the initial set up to daily operation, these systems typically have intuitive interfaces and clear instructions, making them easy to access. Users can manage access permissions, monitor activity and respond to security incidents with just a few clicks. Most systems also allow for changes to be made remotely, providing flexibility and convenience for managers and administrators. While access control systems are packed with advanced features and capabilities, you don’t need to be a tech expert to manage them effectively.

mainEntity.name: How much area does an access control system cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: Access control systems are known for their scalability. These systems can be tailored to your specific needs, irrespective of the size or type of your facility. From small businesses with a single access point to large multi-site corporations, an access control system can cover areas of varying sizes. It’s not only about the number of doors either. The system can also regulate access to lifts, parking lots and any other areas you wish to secure.

mainEntity.name: What are the benefits of an access control system?

acceptedAnswer.text:
There are many advantages of having an access control system in your facility, making it an invaluable addition to your security framework. Most importantly, access control systems provide enhanced security, giving you control over who can access your facility and when. This greatly enhances your security, keeping unauthorised individuals out while ensuring the right people have access when they need it. By preventing unauthorised access, it reduces the likelihood of theft, vandalism or other security incidents. Employees and visitors alike can feel safe knowing access to the facility is carefully managed and monitored.


An access control system also allows for improved monitoring, offering valuable insights into the movement of people within your facility. This visibility can be instrumental for a variety of reasons such as investigating security incidents, improving operational efficiency or ensuring regulatory compliance. These systems are also very convenient, replacing traditional keys for a card or your fingerprint. Whether you want to boost security, gain better control or simply make life easier for everyone on site, an access control system is your solution to achieving all these and more.

mainEntity.name: Can an access control system be integrated with other security systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. access control systems can often be integrated with a variety of other security systems like CCTV surveillance, intruder alarms and fire detection systems. This interconnectivity can create a holistic, robust security infrastructure. For instance, if an access control system denies entry to an individual, this event can trigger the surveillance system to focus on this area, giving you a comprehensive view of what’s happening. Similarly, integration with a fire detection system can enable automatic unlocking of all doors during an emergency, allowing for quick evacuation.

mainEntity.name: Is an alarm system a worthwhile investment?

mainEntity.name: Do alarm systems really work as a deterrent?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many cases, a visible alarm system will act as a deterrent against potential intruders or burglars. This is because intruders gravitate towards properties with weaker security support as there is less chance of being caught.

mainEntity.name: How much do alarm systems cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost of an alarm system depends on various factors such as the type and size of the property, the number of entry points that need to be secured and any additional features or customisations. We offer competitive prices for our alarm systems and can provide a free consultation and quote based on your specific needs.

mainEntity.name: Will installing a security system decrease my insurance premiums?

acceptedAnswer.text: Though it may vary between insurance providers, many providers will decrease the premium of your insurance if you install an alarm system on your premises or property. This is because having an alarm system is viewed as an additional source of security. Of course, this depends on a number of other factors including the location and value of your property.

mainEntity.name: How often should my alarm system be tested?

mainEntity.name: What does a commercial locksmith do?

acceptedAnswer.text: A commercial locksmith works with businesses, body corporates, retail stores, offices, warehouses and other commercial sites to keep their premises secure through professional lock, key and access solutions tailored to each property. A specialist commercial locksmith on the Gold Coast or commercial locksmith in Brisbane can design and install master key systems so you can control who accesses different areas, upgrade old locks to high-security hardware, rekey existing locks after staff changes, repair doors and locks after break-ins and integrate electronic security such as access control and alarms to support your wider security strategy. They also work closely with business owners and facility managers to conduct security assessments, recommend practical improvements, and ensure your property meets insurance and safety requirements.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer emergency commercial locksmith services?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we provide 24/7 emergency commercial locksmith services for businesses across the Gold Coast, Brisbane and Northern NSW, with mobile technicians ready to attend your site when something goes wrong outside normal hours. If you are locked out of your workplace, have a damaged or jammed lock, need to secure your building after a break-in or urgently change locks or rekey after lost or stolen keys, an emergency commercial locksmith on the Gold Coast or commercial locksmith in Brisbane can respond quickly with fully equipped vans to restore access and secure your premises on the spot. Their emergency service is supported by a central contact number, rapid dispatch and experience in handling everything from simple lockouts to complex multi-site properties, so when you’re searching for a reliable locksmith near you in a crisis, you know help is available around the clock.

mainEntity.name: Do you install electronic access control systems for businesses?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in addition to traditional locks and keys, SPL Security Solutions designs and installs electronic access control systems for commercial and industrial sites, integrating them with broader security solutions where required. A commercial locksmith on the Gold Coast or commercial locksmith in Brisbane can supply and configure card readers, keypads, fobs and credential-based access, set up tiered permissions so different staff can only access authorised areas, and link access control with alarms, CCTV and other electronic security platforms to give you better visibility and control over who enters your building and when. They work with leading electronic security brands and can scale systems for single-site offices, multi-storey buildings and large facilities, making them the ideal locksmith near you if you want to modernise your business security and move away from easily lost or copied keys.

mainEntity.name: What types of commercial locks and hardware can you repair or replace?

acceptedAnswer.text: A commercial locksmith can repair, rekey and replace a wide range of locks and hardware commonly found in business premises, including high-security cylinder locks, mortice locks, deadbolts, door closers, panic bars, restricted key systems, master key suites, padlocks, window locks and specialty hardware for glass doors, aluminium shopfronts and fire-rated doors. The team at SPL Security Solutions, for example, supplies and services both decorative and heavy-duty commercial door hardware. They can upgrade older locks to more secure options, replace damaged or worn components, and integrate new locks into an existing master key or restricted key system, ensuring consistent key control throughout the system. Whether you operate on the Gold Coast or in Brisbane, a commercial locksmith can work across offices, retail tenancies, warehouses, strata properties and more to keep doors operating smoothly and securely.

mainEntity.name: Do you provide ongoing maintenance for commercial security systems?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we support businesses with ongoing maintenance for both physical locks and electronic security systems, helping you maintain compliance, reliability, and effectiveness over time. A commercial locksmith on the Gold Coast or in Brisbane can schedule routine inspections of your locks, master key systems, door hardware, safes and restricted keys, as well as service electronic access control, alarms and CCTV in partnership with their electronic security technicians, ensuring early detection of faults before they become security risks. They can also review your site after staff changes, tenancy changes or incidents, update access permissions, rekey locks where necessary and recommend upgrades as technology and standards evolve, so you always have a dependable locksmith who understands your site and provides proactive, not just reactive, commercial security support.

mainEntity.name: What is a restricted or security key?

acceptedAnswer.text: A restricted key is a key that can only be cut by an authorised locksmith with authority from an authorised person who manages the key system.

mainEntity.name: How does the restriction work?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Restricted keys are designed by a manufacturer who registers or patents the design of the key to prevent copying. The manufacturer then sets terms to the Locksmithing industry on how the keys can be used. This comes in 3 levels:


  • Level 1 is factory-restricted so only the manufacturer can acquire.
  • Level 2 is locksmith-restricted, where only approved locksmiths can acquire specific profiles of the key design.
  • Level 3 is open broach where any locksmith can acquire the profile of the keys.

mainEntity.name: Can I transfer my system to another locksmith?

acceptedAnswer.text:
It is possible to have a restricted system transferred between locksmiths. However, this requires the receiving locksmith to have or be able to have the profile of key that the system is on.


For example, if the system is on an open broach, then it can be transferred to any locksmith who has the profile. However, if the system is on an exclusive profile, then the system cannot be transferred as the manufacturer has agreed to only allow that locksmith to have that profile of key. In this example, if a transfer was needed, then it is possible to contact the factory and arrange for the system to be factory-controlled.

mainEntity.name: What happens when the patent/registered design expires?

acceptedAnswer.text: When the patent or design registration expires, the legal protection against copying the keys expires as well. The majority of Australian locksmiths are members of a security group, like the Master Locksmiths Association of Australia and New Zealand or the Locksmith Guild of Australia where the bylaws of membership continue to protect the security of keys after the patents or registrations expire. It is still recommended that by the time of the expiry, an upgrade should be considered.

mainEntity.name: How do signatories work?

acceptedAnswer.text: A signatory is a person who is authorised to make requests and place orders relating to the restricted system. A signatory can be anyone from owners, managers, caretakers and body corporates to company representatives. When the system is set up a registration form is supplied and once returned completed, the persons listed on the registration are added as the authorities to manage the system. Only persons on the authority list can order extra keys or works for the system.

mainEntity.name: How much do restricted keys cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Our company charges a set price for restricted keys. Once sold to the customer, they are the property of the purchaser, who has the right to use them as they wish, including reselling them at a higher price.

mainEntity.name: Why do I need permission to change a lock or get keys?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most circumstances, the system has been set up for an entire premise or building. This means the authorities on the system are responsible for the security and maintenance of the key system for the location and must be aware of any changes. The signatories are the people in charge of the system. The locksmith must abide by their directions.

mainEntity.name: What if I have different keys for the same building? Why can I order some keys but not others?

acceptedAnswer.text: Restricted systems can be set up in a number of ways including limiting the authority of the signatories. This can be in the form of requiring multiple signatories to authorise keys or only allowing for certain signatories to be able to order certain keys but not others. It could also be that there are multiple systems established in the location that are controlled by different persons. An example of this would be a high rise where the body corporate and management have separate systems for the units they manage, though they are in the same building and work together. If the signatories for management are not signatories for the body corporate’s system, the locksmith cannot provide much in the way of information to the managers about the body corporate’s system as they are not authorised, and vice versa for the body corporate on the management system.

mainEntity.name: Why as an owner can I not get keys?

acceptedAnswer.text: This would be due to the listed signatories. In the case of a unit in a complex or a high rise, most systems are controlled by either building management or the body corporate as they are responsible for the maintenance of the security and the doors of the building. In the case of a business owner this would be the way the system was set up.

mainEntity.name: How can the signatories be changed?

acceptedAnswer.text: The signatories on a system can be changed by submitting a Signatory Registration Form to the locksmith requesting changes to be made. The registration form contains instructions on how the form needs to be completed. Regardless of whether a signatory has left the company/premises, unless they are removed from the signatory list they are still listed as an authority on the system.

mainEntity.name: How can CCTV improve home security?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can’t put a price on your family’s safety. Installing a CCTV security system is an extremely effective way to protect your home. A security camera system is a powerful deterrent against potential criminal activity. If a crime does take place, you will have video evidence of the act which can prove helpful in a police investigation. CCTV also has other practical uses. For instance, your CCTV system provides live video footage to ensure your elderly relatives, children and pets are safe.

mainEntity.name: Do I need CCTV for my business?

acceptedAnswer.text: Regardless of the size of your business, CCTV security cameras are a valuable investment. Not only do they serve as a powerful deterrent to criminal activity, but their benefits extend far beyond security. CCTV systems help improve inventory control, enhances staff and customer safety and prevent issues like employee theft or fraud. In the event of an injury or accident, having video footage makes filing a claim much easier and more straightforward. With a CCTV system in place, you’re not only enhancing security but also protecting your bottom line.

mainEntity.name: Should I install a wired or wireless security system?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wireless security cameras are popular for their easy installation and the convenience of being able to disconnect from your Wi-Fi network. However, they can be challenging to maintain. Many wireless systems rely on batteries for power, which means you'll need to replace or recharge them periodically and they are prone to dropping out in a weak Wi-Fi signal. To ensure consistent performance and greater reliability, we recommend opting for a wired CCTV system, which eliminates these concerns and provides a more stable, long-term solution.

mainEntity.name: How do I pick the right camera type?

acceptedAnswer.text:
We have a wide variety of security camera systems available. Some of the most popular security camera types include:

  • Dome
  • Pignose
  • Bullet
  • Panoramic
  • Motorised PTZ cameras

Each CCTV camera is best suited to different applications. So, we recommend speaking to our team. We will help you find the ideal camera to suit your needs.

mainEntity.name: Will moving trees trigger a recording?

acceptedAnswer.text: Moving trees could potentially trigger a recording, especially if the camera's sensitivity is high. To resolve this, adjusting the camera's motion detection settings to ignore small movements, like those caused by trees, can be effective. Alternatively, repositioning the camera away from the trees or using physical barriers to block their movement in the camera's field of view can prevent unnecessary recordings.

mainEntity.name: Can I view the camera footage remotely?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with most modern systems, you no longer need to be onsite to review the CCTV camera footage. If you have a reliable internet connection, no matter where you are, you can view the day’s footage. Everything your security system records can be accessed via a free and easy to use app. This app is available through your PC, tablet or smartphone.
